name: Viersche
description: Viersche (Hundert/Hunderte) is a Black Forest German partnership trick-taking game. 4 players in 2 teams. 36-card deck. 9 cards each. Bottom card = trump. Forehand MUST lead trump first trick (if no trumps, lead face-down). Race to 100+ card points. First to claim 100 wins; erase 4 'rungs' to win session.

history.origins: Viersche (also Hundert or Hunderte) is a point-trick game local to the Wolf and Kinzig valleys in the Black Forest of Germany. It was first recorded on a 1932 map of the most common card games in Baden, republished in Friedrich Schlager's 1951 article on Cego; the centre of play was the Wolf valley, with other clusters near Oberharmersbach, Baiersbronn, St. Georgen, Villingen and Geisingen. It is the forward version of Hindersche (Swabian: viersche = forwards, hindersche = backwards), which was played by foresters, farmers and journeymen in the old Principality of Fürstenberg; anticlockwise play and the ranking of the ten suggest the game may be two or three centuries old. It is likely a descendant of Réunion, a German game once popular in the Rhineland and along the Neckar. Since at least 2003, annual tournaments have been held around Epiphany in Bad Rippoldsau.
